meta.tagline: City of the cliffs: orange blossom, ancient theatres and a waterfall that falls into the sea

pills: A city whose waterfall falls into the sea
Ski in the morning, swim at noon — possible

overview.title: Welcome to Antalya
overview.intro: Whoever thinks Antalya is merely a 'resort town' changes their mind at the first glance over the cliffs: the Taurus mountains drop sheer into blue water, the Ottoman lanes of Kaleiçi lean against Roman walls, and the city's waterfall pours forty metres straight into the Mediterranean. Bitter-orange trees shade the pavements, and concerts still play in two-thousand-year-old theatres. This city finds work for your beach towel and your hiking boots in the same weekend — here the Mediterranean is not just a sea but a way of living.

local_word.definition: The coastal cliffs that are Antalya's signature: the city is built atop these sheer travertine bluffs. Walking the cliff parks is the Antalyan evening ritual — the sea foams below while the Beydağları turn violet on the horizon.

rules.title: Tour by the hour, not the season
rules.description: The midday summer sun is serious: set the ancient cities and Kaleiçi for morning, the sea for afternoon, the cliff walk for sunset. An Antalya day is lived in three shifts — whoever argues with the heat surrenders in the shade.

rules.title: Don't try to drive into Kaleiçi
rules.description: The old town's narrow lanes belong to walkers: leave the car in the outer car parks and enter through the walls on foot. Getting lost is no problem — every slope ends at the marina or in a café courtyard.

rules.title: Never skip the ancient cities
rules.description: Antalya's radius is an open-air museum: Perge, Aspendos, Termessos and Phaselis are each an hour away. Add at least one ancient city to the beach programme — on this coast, history comes before sand.

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: Multilingual life in the tourist zones

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: The waterfall pours straight into the sea

tip.label: The Antalya philosophy
tip.text: The Antalyan's clock is set to sunset: tea in the cliff park, simit at the foot of the Hıdırlık Tower, last light over the marina. End your day's plan not at evening but at sundown — the rest is detail.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The centre is solved by tram and foot; a wheel or a tour opens the ancient cities and coves, and the coastal buses cover the beaches.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.description: AYT sits close to town: the AntRay tram connects the airport to the centre, and taxis and transfers reach Kaleiçi in half an hour. Buy the AntalyaKart at the first stop — the single key to bus and tram.

items.title: The tram — two lines, two characters
items.description: The modern AntRay crosses the city end to end; the single-car nostalgic tram sways from the Kaleiçi gate towards Konyaaltı. The second is less transport than pleasure — take the window seat.

items.title: Kaleiçi and the cliff parks on foot
items.description: The Kaleiçi labyrinth, Karaalioğlu Park and the clifftop paths are the city's finest routes: the marina descent is steep, the return patient. Comfortable shoes, water and a hat are the summer standard.

items.title: The beach and waterfall lines
items.description: City buses run regularly to Konyaaltı and Lara beaches, and a line serves the Düden falls. Riding the bus with a beach bag is daily life in this city — no shyness needed; the locals do the same.

items.title: A rental car — the key to the ancient cities
items.description: Four wheels are the way to tour Perge, Aspendos, Termessos and Phaselis at your own rhythm: roads good, signs clear. The Termessos mountain road is full of bends — set out in the morning cool.

callout.label: Cable car tip
callout.text: Ride the Tünektepe cable car to 600 metres: Konyaaltı's curve, the cliffs and the Beydağları in one frame. Go up an hour before sunset — on the way down you catch the city lights from above.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Antalya the question is clear: Kaleiçi's stone courtyard, Konyaaltı's mountain-backed sea, or Lara's sand?

local_word.definition: The heart of a Kaleiçi mansion: the cool inner garden with its bitter-orange trees and cistern. Choosing a boutique hotel in Antalya is really choosing a courtyard — breakfast happens there, the evening glass happens there, and it is the refuge of the hot day.

items.name: Kaleiçi
items.description: Boutique hotels converted from Ottoman mansions, each with a courtyard: marina, walls and historic lanes at your door. Bar sounds may drift in on summer nights — the price of atmosphere, with morning silence as the reward.

items.name: Konyaaltı
items.description: Modern hotels and apartments behind the pebble beach at the foot of the Beydağları: mountains in the morning, sea views at night. With its beach promenade and bike path, the city's airiest shore.

items.name: Lara and Kundu
items.description: A long sandy beach and the big all-inclusive hotels: the classic for families and beach-first holidaymakers. The distance from the centre is balanced by hotel comfort — city sightseers should budget for wheels.

items.name: The centre — Işıklar and Muratpaşa
items.description: The Antalyan's daily life of cafés, patisseries and market streets: walking distance to Kaleiçi, prices below the tourist front line. For touring the city by living it.

items.name: Çıralı
items.description: A quiet guesthouse village an hour away, on a turtle-nesting beach: neighbour to the Olympos ruins and the Chimaera flames. The address for living Antalya from nature rather than from a base.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Antalya's sun calendar is generous: spring and autumn gold, summer a heat exam, and winter the season of the 'ski in the morning, swim at noon' legend.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Orange Blossom Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Blossom scent, the sea warming up
items.description: The city smells of orange blossom, the ancient sites turn green, and the sea warms with May. The crowds are still on their way and everything is open — this is Antalya's most balanced window.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: Come in early April: the bitter-orange blossom wraps the whole city and the cliff parks are in flower. These are also the year's coolest, most comfortable weeks for walking the ancient cities.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Hot Peak
items.subtitle: Summer · Noons racing to 40 degrees, long beach evenings
items.description: The heat is serious and the humidity joins it: life splits into morning, sea, and air-conditioned noon. The sea is magnificent and the evenings long — festivals and open-air concerts pass into history at Aspendos.

callout.label: July note
callout.text: In summer squeeze the ancient-city visit into 8-11 am and give noon to the sea or the museum. Whoever tries Termessos at a summer midday goes one-on-one with the sun on a mountain — water, hat and the early hour are non-negotiable.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Warmest Sea
items.subtitle: Autumn · The September-October sea peak, softening air
items.description: The sea returns its stored summer heat in September and October: the swimming season stretches to November, the crowds recede, and the light becomes photographer's light. Those who know Antalya book for these months.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October both swim and walk the Antalya stages of the Lycian Way: the air is made for hiking and the sea still warm. This is the year's best 'two worlds at once' month.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Green Winter and Saklıkent
items.subtitle: Winter · Mild sunny days, ski season in the mountains
items.description: Winter is gentle in Antalya: on sunny days you drink tea in the cliff park in a jacket while the orange harvest paints the city. Up in the Beydağları, the Saklıkent ski season opens — the city legend is true.

callout.label: March tip
callout.text: In late March test the legend yourself: skiing at Saklıkent in the morning, 20-degree sunshine in the city at noon, and a dip in the sea if you dare. Same day, same city — nobody will believe your photos.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Antalya's cooking is the meeting of the Mediterranean and the Yörük table: tahini piyaz, skewers over coals, fresh-squeezed orange juice and the harbour fish houses.

local_word.definition: Antalya's signature meze: the thick meeting of tahini, cumin, chilli flakes and lemon. It reaches the table first and is wiped up with bread — by Antalyan lights, whoever skimps on the cumin has lost from the start.

items.name: Tahini piyaz — the city's signature
items.description: The Antalya piyaz marries white beans with tahini: garlicky, sharp with vinegar, crowned with egg. Think of it not as the köfte's side dish but as the lead role — in this city piyaz is identity, not garnish.

items.name: Şiş köfte and tandır
items.description: Hand-pressed köfte skewers over coals and tandır lamb slow-cooked in a pit: the lunchtime pride of the tradesmen's lokantas. With hibeş, sliced tomato and charred pepper — the Mediterranean grill table.
items.tag: At an esnaf lokantası · with hibeş

items.name: The harbour fish houses
items.description: The gulf's daily catch is chosen from the counter at the marina and fishing-harbour restaurants: grouper, bream, amberjack in season. A clifftop sunset table adds the view to the bill — choose it knowingly.
items.tag: Choose from the counter · time it for sunset

items.name: The orange and citrus stalls
items.description: The orange is this city's coat of arms: a fresh-squeezed glass, bitter-orange jam at the market, orchards glowing on the branch in winter. If you hunt orange-blossom honey in March, head for the bazaar.
items.tag: Fresh squeezed · jam from the market

items.name: Yörük breakfast and gözleme
items.description: A tradition come down from the mountain pastures: griddle-baked gözleme, goat's cheese, olives and tea over a wood fire. The breakfast gardens on the Geyikbayırı road are the weekend classic.
items.tag: At the weekend · in a highland garden

items.name: Bici bici and the cooling sweets
items.description: Shaved ice, starch pudding and rose syrup: bici bici is the street invention of Mediterranean heat. With karsambaç and ice cream alongside — the official coolants of a summer afternoon.

callout.label: The table rule
callout.text: On the tourist front line the 'fish + view' price doubles: choose the counter-fronted, daily-board, local-filled place instead. At the piyaz house the rule is simple — go at noon; a good pot never survives to mid-afternoon.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone tours Kaleiçi; these six are Antalya's backstage.

items.name: The Lower Düden — off the Lara cliff
items.description: The Düden water pours forty metres off the cliff straight into the Mediterranean: one of the world's few waterfalls that fall into the sea. Watch it from a boat or from the park above — at sunset the water flies golden.

items.name: Termessos
items.description: An ancient city built into a mountain cleft at a thousand metres: its theatre's backstage is a precipice, its audience the clouds. The city Alexander gave up on taking — the climb costs sweat, the reward is Türkiye's most dramatic ancient view.

items.name: Perge
items.description: A Roman city of stadium, colonnaded avenue and fountains: at the first hour of morning it is nearly empty. Pair it with the statues in the Antalya Museum — the stones are here, their faces are there.

items.name: The Hıdırlık Tower and the Karaalioğlu sunset
items.description: The foot of the Roman tower is the city's sunset box: cliffs, gulf and the Beydağları in one frame. The simit seller passes, the tea arrives, the sun drops behind Konyaaltı — Antalya's most democratic show.

items.name: Yanartaş (the Chimaera)
items.description: On the slope above Çıralı, flames have seeped from the rock for thousands of years, dying and relighting: this is mythology's Chimaera. Climb after dark — flame, stars and sea enter the same frame.

items.rarity: The stairway coves of the cliffs
items.name: The cliff beaches — Mermerli to Adalar
items.description: Rocky coves inside the city, reached by stairs: Mermerli's historic jetty, Adalar's stone platforms. Not sand — but the clearest water in town, and the locals' lunchtime swim.

callout.label: Museum tip
callout.text: Tour the Antalya Museum after the ancient cities, not before: meeting the gods of Perge's avenue in the statue hall after walking that avenue completes the story. The mid-afternoon hours are quietest.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Antalya knows tourism well — and its games too: recognise these four and your budget and day stay intact.

items.name: The priceless 'welcome, friend' in Kaleiçi
items.description: At some tables reached via doorway invitations on the old town's busy lanes, the price reveals itself only on the bill.
items.instead: Never sit at a table without written prices; choose the courtyard places with local customers. The two-streets-in rule holds in Kaleiçi too.

items.name: Mistaking the beach club for the beach
items.description: Some operations on Konyaaltı and Lara turn a beach day into a swollen bill with sunbeds + minimum spends.
items.instead: The public beach sections are free and it is the same sea: spread your towel, take your tea from the kiosk. Choose a beach club deliberately for music and comfort, never by default.

items.name: The loudspeaker 'pirate' boat tour
items.description: Giant party boats tour the coves in convoy: swimming stops short, crowds high.
items.instead: Pick a small boat or private tour and ask the route and swim times before boarding. If you want a silent cove, take the first morning departure — coves prefer morning people too.

items.name: The airport-hotel transfer game
items.description: In some vehicles boarded at the kerb without a price, the distance is short and the figure a surprise.
items.instead: Use the tram + short taxi combination, or a transfer with the price written in advance. In town, an app-hailed taxi always beats kerbside bargaining.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Antalya's costliest mistake is building the plan on the midday sun: invest your energy, like your money, in morning and evening. Sea at noon, history at dawn, cliffs at dusk — break that order and you meet only half the city.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A Mediterranean day from walls to cliffs

steps.title: A Kaleiçi morning
steps.description: Enter by Hadrian's Gate, lose yourself around the Broken Minaret and the mansion lanes; descend to the marina for the first tea above the harbour — the crowds still asleep.

steps.title: The Antalya Museum or Perge
steps.description: Either face Rome in the museum's statue halls, or drive half an hour and walk Perge's colonnaded avenue: the morning cool belongs to history.

steps.title: A piyaz + köfte lunch
steps.description: Tahini piyaz, şiş köfte and hibeş at a tradesmen's lokanta: Antalya's signature table. Fresh-squeezed orange juice on top.

steps.title: The sea shift
steps.description: A mountain-view swim at Konyaaltı or city-centre cool in Mermerli's stairway cove: the afternoon belongs to the water.

steps.title: The Karaalioğlu sunset
steps.description: Walk the cliff park and take your place at the Hıdırlık Tower: as the sun drops behind the Beydağları, the gulf turns to gold.

steps.title: Evening in Kaleiçi
steps.description: Dinner in a courtyard, then a night walk above the marina: lamplight on stone lanes, boat lights on the water — a Mediterranean day closes like this.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: City, antiquity and nature — three Antalyas

steps.title: Classic Antalya
steps.description: The one-day flow above: Kaleiçi, museum/Perge, piyaz, sea, sunset.

steps.title: The antiquity tour
steps.description: Climb early to Termessos's mountain theatre; stand on Aspendos's stage in the afternoon; watch the Lower Düden pour into the sea on the way back; the day's catch at a harbour fish house at night.

steps.title: Nature and farewell
steps.description: Escape to the Çıralı-Olympos line: ruins and the turtle beach in the morning, the sea in the afternoon, the Chimaera flames after dark. One last bici bici on the road home — let the farewell be cool.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: The language of Mediterranean hospitality is warm; these five words open every table.

items.meaning: The heart of the welcome — answered with 'hoş bulduk'; together they open doors
The table's opening and closing — you'll hear it when the piyaz arrives
The finest thanks to the cook — the sentence that makes the master smile
The casual thank-you — used alongside the tea glass
The hopeful goodbye — on the Mediterranean it counts as a promise, not a parting
